He turns to one student. "What would you do in a case like this?"

The student thinks. "Well," he says, "I suppose I'd limp, too."

title: The Talking Scale
text:
Nathan arrives early at the train station and notices a new talking scale on the platform. He steps on, puts in a dollar, and the scale says, "You weigh 160 pounds, and you are Jewish." Nathan is astonished.

He pays again. "You weigh 160 pounds, you are Jewish, and you are waiting for the 7:35 train to your job at the bank." Now he is determined to fool it.

In the restroom he messes up his hair, puts on dark glasses, takes off his tie, drapes his jacket over his arm and sticks a bandage on his chin. He steps back on the scale and pays a third dollar.

"You still weigh 160 pounds, and you are still Jewish," says the scale. "And you're a shlimazel, a very unlucky fellow. You just missed your train."

title: Justice Prevailed
text:
A junior partner in a law firm is sent abroad to defend a long-time client accused of robbery. After days of trial, the client is acquitted and released.

Thrilled, the young lawyer emails the firm: "Justice prevailed!"

The senior partner replies at once: "Appeal immediately."

title: The First Step to Forgiveness
text:
A teacher finishes her lesson for the children and wants to be sure they got the point. "Can anyone tell me what you must do before you can be forgiven?"

There is a short pause. Then a small boy in the back raises his hand. "Sin," he says.

title: Forty Dinners for 103 Passengers
text:
Half an hour into an evening flight, the flight attendant announces nervously, "I'm so sorry, there has been a catering mistake. We have 103 passengers and only 40 dinners."

When the grumbling quiets down, she adds, "Anyone kind enough to give up their meal so that someone else can eat will receive free drinks for the rest of the flight."

Ninety minutes later she announces, "If anyone would like to change their mind, we still have forty dinners."

title: Guess Who Sent Them
text:
Abe and Rachel Katz have just married and moved into a New York apartment, filled with their precious wedding gifts. One day two tickets to a popular show arrive in the mail. On the envelope is one line: "Guess who sent them."

They assume it is a late wedding present and enjoy the show, spending the whole evening trying to figure out who sent it.

When they get home, the apartment has been emptied of every wedding gift and everything of value. On the bare dining-room table lies a note: "Now you know!"

title: The Perfect Dinner Guest
text:
A beggar asks a well-dressed gentleman for two dollars. "You won't spend it on liquor, will you?" "No sir, I don't drink." "Not on a card game?" "No, I don't gamble." "On golf fees?" "I don't play golf." "On fishing gear?" "I don't fish."

The gentleman immediately invites him home for a hot meal. The beggar gladly accepts. On the way, he asks, "Won't your wife be upset to see a guy like me at her table?"

"Probably," says the gentleman. "But it will be worth it. I want her to see what a man turns out like when he doesn't drink, gamble, fish or play golf!"

title: Who Pushed Me?
text:
A millionaire who collects live alligators keeps them in a pool behind his mansion. He also has a single, beautiful daughter. At a big party he announces, "To any man who can swim across this pool and come out unharmed, I will give a million dollars or my daughter!"

He has hardly finished when there is a huge splash. A man is swimming with all his might, the crowd cheering, and he reaches the other side unharmed.

"Incredible!" says the millionaire. "I never thought it could be done. So, which do you want, the million or my daughter?"

The man catches his breath. "I don't want your money, and I don't want your daughter. I want to know who pushed me in!"

title: A Year's Subscription
text:
Rabbi Friedman asks Esther how things are going with her mother.

"She's a difficult person, Rabbi," says Esther, and tells him all the problems. Then she sighs. "Well, we all have issues."

"Issues?" says the rabbi. "From what you describe, your mother has a year's subscription."

title: The Lost Kiddush Cup
text:
At a bar mitzvah, the boy's parents give him a valuable silver kiddush cup, a family heirloom. After the celebration, the cup vanishes. They search everywhere, with no luck.

Many years later, at the young man's wedding, the family mentions to the rabbi that the special cup is a family tradition at weddings, and that it was lost after the bar mitzvah.

"When exactly did you lose it?"

"Right after the bar mitzvah."

"Where did you put it?"

"In a safe place, in the bar mitzvah boy's tefillin bag."

They looked, and there it was. The boy had not opened his tefillin bag since his bar mitzvah.

title: Button It, Sir
text:
The colonel who serves as inspector general is very particular about uniforms. One day he spots a junior airman with something out of place.

"Airman," he bellows, "what do you do when a shirt pocket is unbuttoned?"

"Button it, sir!"

The colonel looks him in the eye. "Well?"

The airman nervously reaches over and buttons the colonel's shirt pocket.

title: The Hammer Throw
text:
The hammer throw final comes down to three athletes: a soldier, a farmer, and Larry, who still lives with his parents.

The soldier throws 85 meters. "I come from a military family," he tells reporters. "It gives me discipline." The farmer throws 88. "I come from a farming family. It gives me strength."

Larry hurls the hammer 95 meters and wins the gold. "I come from a long line of lazy people," he explains. "They taught me that if anyone ever puts a hammer in your hand, throw it as far away as you can."

title: The Debt Collector
text:
A man starts working at a debt collection agency. His colleagues tell him about one impossible case, a man who has owed money for years. Within days, the newcomer collects the entire sum.

"How did you do it?" they ask, astounded.

"Very simple. I told him that if he didn't pay, I'd tell all his other creditors that he had already paid us."

title: Miss Cohen's Indigestion
text:
The old family doctor goes on vacation and leaves his practice to his son, a newly graduated physician. When the father returns, the young man proudly reports, among other things, that he cured Miss Cohen, an elderly, wealthy lady, of her chronic indigestion.

"My boy," says the old doctor, "I'm proud of you. But Miss Cohen's indigestion is what put you through college."

title: The Jews and the Chimneysweeps
text:
After a terrible attack on the Tsar in Russia, a government official in a Ukrainian town addresses the local rabbi threateningly. "I suppose you know exactly who was behind it."

"Oh, I have no idea," says the rabbi. "But the government's conclusion will be the same as always. They will blame the Jews and the chimneysweeps."

"The chimneysweeps?" asks the puzzled official. "Why the chimneysweeps?"

"Why the Jews?" says the rabbi.

title: A Second Helping of Soup
text: A man is invited to dinner at a friend's. The friend gives him some advice. "If they serve you soup and it's delicious, take a second helping when it's offered, because the rest of the meal may not be as good. And if the soup is awful, take a second helping anyway, because the rest may be worse!"

title: The Cup That Had a Baby
text:
Fenster the clever beggar decides to outwit Eisinger the rich miser. He borrows a silver cup, and the next day returns it with a small extra cup. "Your cup gave birth overnight, so it's only right that you have the baby." The miser thinks, "What a fool," and gladly accepts.

Fenster then borrows a silver candelabra and returns it with a little candlestick: another birth. Delighted, the miser hands over his diamond-studded gold watch.

This time Fenster doesn't return it. Weeks later the miser comes to demand it. "I'm so sorry," says Fenster. "Your watch took sick and died."

"Ridiculous!" "Why? If a cup and a candelabra can have babies, as you agreed, why can't a watch pass away?"

title: Whose Father Is Fastest?
text:
Three boys in the schoolyard are bragging about their fathers.

"My father is the fastest," says the first. "He shoots an arrow and starts running, and he gets there before the arrow."

"That's nothing," says the second. "My father is a hunter. He fires his gun and he's there before the bullet."

The third boy shakes his head. "You two know nothing about fast. My father works for the government. He finishes at 4:30, and he's home by 3:45!"

title: Hiding His Teeth
text:
Two elderly ladies, Ruth and Naomi, talk about their husbands over tea.

"I wish my Ernie would stop biting his nails," says Ruth. "It makes me so nervous."

"My Shlomi used to do the same," says Naomi. "But I cured him."

"How? I've tried everything. I even asked my son-in-law, the doctor, and nothing worked!"

Naomi answers with the wisdom of her years. "I hid his teeth."

title: The Car Pete Built
text:
Two coworkers sit down for lunch in the office cafeteria. "Whatever happened to Pete in payroll?"

"He got a crazy idea to build a brand-new kind of car."

"How?"

"He took an engine from a Volvo, tires from a Porsche, seats from a Land Rover, mirrors from a Tesla, and, well, you get the idea."

"So what did he end up with?"

"Ten years in prison."

title: Would You Tie My Shoe?
text:
A police officer is taking a vandalism report at an elementary school when a little girl of about six interrupts. She looks him up and down. "Are you a cop?"

"Yes," he says, and goes on writing.

"My mother said that if I ever need help, I should ask the police. Is that right?"

"Yes, that's right."

"Well, then," she says, and sticks out her foot. "Would you please tie my shoe?"

title: You Lose Ten, I Lose Ten
text:
Abe says to his friend Willie, "Lend me twenty dollars."

Willie takes out his wallet and hands over a ten.

"I asked for twenty!"

"I know," says Willie. "This way you lose ten and I lose ten."

A thought for the days of awe: we can't fool G-d. Let's make resolutions we can actually keep, and be honest and real when we pray.

title: You Have Your Friends
text:
Moishe Finkelstein, a tailor from a small Ukrainian village, applies for membership in the Communist Party in Kiev.

"Who was Karl Marx?" asks the official. "Never heard of him."

"Who is Stalin?" "Never met him."

"Who was Lenin?" "Can't say I recall the name."

"Are you taking us for fools?"

"Not for a moment, Comrade. Do you know Yossel Feigenbaum?" "No." "Mendele Levinsky?" "No." "Shpilkey Beazly?" "Never heard of him."

"Well," says Finkelstein, "that's how it is. You have your friends and I have mine."

title: Now It's Your Turn to Call
text:
Soviet Union, 1930s. The phone rings at KGB headquarters.

"Is this the KGB? I'm calling to report my neighbor, Yankel Rabinovitz, an enemy of the state. He is hiding diamonds in his firewood."

"This will be noted."

The next day, agents arrive at Yankel's house, search the shed, split every log, find no diamonds, curse at him and leave.

The phone rings at Yankel's house. "Hello, Yankel! Did the KGB come?"

"Yes."

"Did they chop all your firewood?"

"They did."

"Good. Now it's your turn to call. I need my vegetable patch plowed."

title: Ten Rolls of Wallpaper
text:
Shirley decides to wallpaper her bedroom, but isn't sure how many rolls to buy. Her neighbor Debbie just did the same job in an identical room, so she calls her. "Debbie, how many rolls did you buy?"

"Ten."

Shirley buys ten rolls and does the job. When she finishes, two rolls are left over. Puzzled, she calls Debbie again. "I bought ten rolls like you said, and I have two left!"

"Yes," says Debbie. "So did I."

title: Why the Foreman Fired Him
text:
Two neighbors are talking about work. "Say, why did your foreman fire you?"

"Well, you know how a foreman spends his day standing around, watching other people work. My foreman got jealous. People started thinking I was the foreman."

title: The Neighbor and the Groceries
text:
A little old lady steps onto her porch every morning, raises her arms and shouts, "Praise the Lord!" A new neighbor, an atheist, is annoyed, and every morning he steps out and shouts, "There is no Lord!"

One cold winter morning she calls out, "Praise the Lord! I have no food and I'm hungry. Please provide for me!" The next morning, two big bags of groceries sit on her porch.

"Praise the Lord!" she cries. "He has provided groceries!"

Her neighbor jumps out of the hedge. "There is no Lord! I bought those groceries!"

She raises her arms again. "Praise the Lord! He sent me groceries and made the devil pay for them!"

title: Is This Abe?
text:
The phone rings. "Hello, is that you, Abe?"

"Yes, this is Abe."

"It doesn't sound like Abe."

"Well, it's Abe all right."

"You're sure it's Abe?"

"Absolutely."

"Well, listen, Abe, this is Moe. Can you lend me fifty pounds?"

"When Abe comes in, I'll tell him you called."
